xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4477: Shared Sessions v0 (slice 6): read-only terminal channel

plan.title: Shared Sessions v0 (slice 6): read-only terminal channel
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: About 25 files across contracts, dashboard server (pty-hub + sharing), dashboard frontend sharing, one Playwright spec, the frontend test subset list and four doc files. It is one vertical feature: the wire types, host source, peer hub, viewer peer and viewer toggle are useless without each other, and the PRD (PAN-658 slice map) defines this as one slice. The work is still split into 11 independently reviewable items.

narratives.Problem: PAN-4474 created the terminal data channel on every Shared Sessions peer connection but sends nothing on it, and PAN-4475's viewer gives it no listener. The parent PRD's FR-9 requires a viewer to toggle to a read-only live view of the host's terminal, with viewer keystrokes structurally unable to reach the host shell. The PRD assumed a tmux PTY hub always exists; on main, Herdr is the default backend (no PTY hub) and a tmux hub exists only while a /ws/terminal tab is open.
narratives.Proposal: Add a viewer->host 'terminal-watch' control payload and a host->viewer TerminalPayload (snapshot/output/size/unavailable) to the v1 wire format, additively. A new TerminalBridge resolves the shared conversation's terminal per watch: on Herdr one read-only observe stream per watching viewer; on tmux a listener on the PTY hub via a new listener seam in pty-hub.ts, creating the hub at the window's client size when no tab holds it (hub spawn/wiring extracted from ws-terminal.ts into pty-hub-attach.ts). PeerHub attaches a watch only for negotiated peers and still subscribes to no inbound message on the terminal channel. The viewer's WebRtcViewer reads terminal envelopes and sends the watch; a Conversation/Terminal toggle mounts a read-only xterm (disableStdin, no onData, sized to the host). Full design: .pan/drafts/PAN-4477.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Viewer input to the host terminal in any form, including for contributors or the controller
- Any inbound message handler on the host's terminal data channel
- A Herdr viewer following a host resize without re-toggling
- Terminal scrollback history beyond the snapshot
- Sharing any terminal other than the shared conversation's own tmuxSession (no companion terminals, no agent panes)
- Waiting out a conversation respawn during a watch
- Terminal-specific overflow recovery (the existing 64 Mi-character peer close applies)
- Linked-machine (@<machine>) conversations as a share scope
- Any change to the share Worker in services/share/
- Modifying XTerminal.tsx or the /ws/terminal wire protocol
- A bump of the shared wire version

autoDecisions.summary: Herdr hosts stream the terminal through one read-only observeTerminal stream per watching viewer; tmux hosts consume the PTY hub as the issue specifies
autoDecisions.rationale: Herdr is the default backend and has no PTY hub; observe has no write method (read-only by construction) and starts with its own full snapshot. The issue's pty-hub instruction is honoured for tmux.

autoDecisions.summary: On tmux, the bridge creates the PTY hub when no /ws/terminal tab holds one, spawning at window height plus status lines
autoDecisions.rationale: A hub only exists while a tab is open; spawning at the client size keeps the host window size unchanged (NFR-4).

autoDecisions.summary: Rejected a separate 'tmux attach -r -f ignore-size' client per share
autoDecisions.rationale: Live probe on tmux 3.4 (2026-11-03): an ignore-size client resizes the window when it is the only client and the window snaps back to its size after the host's client leaves, a host-visible side effect; it also contradicts the issue's pty-hub instruction.

autoDecisions.summary: The viewer's toggle travels on the control channel as { kind: 'terminal-watch', watch }
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD streams terminal bytes only while a viewer has the view toggled, which needs an inbound request; control is the only channel the host reads, so the terminal channel keeps no inbound handler.

autoDecisions.summary: Terminal content is wrapped in normal SharedEnvelopes with a TerminalPayload
autoDecisions.rationale: Reuses seq gap detection, fragmentation for large snapshots and ChannelWriter backpressure unchanged; payload data is still the raw terminal output.

autoDecisions.summary: A Herdr viewer does not follow host resizes until it re-toggles; a tmux viewer does
autoDecisions.rationale: Herdr observe streams keep their opening size (docs/TERMINAL-BACKENDS.md); the hub notifies listeners of resizes for free.

autoDecisions.summary: The viewer xterm sizes to the host grid with no FitAddon and does not reuse XTerminal.tsx
autoDecisions.rationale: Fitting to the container would re-wrap host output; XTerminal is coupled to /ws/terminal and is on the file-size allowlist.

autoDecisions.summary: Add a Playwright e2e on a real tmux session instead of a werift loopback terminal test
autoDecisions.rationale: It proves both issue acceptance criteria (live output, keystrokes without effect) through real Chromium and stays under the 25-file finalize limit.

Add subscribeToTmuxHub: a read-only, snapshot-first tmux terminal source over the PTY hub

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4. Add TmuxHubDeps {hubs, sessionExists, clientSize, captureViewport, spawn}, productionTmuxHubDeps and subscribeToTmuxHub(sessionName, onFrame: (TerminalFrame) => void, deps?) : Promise<{close()} | null> to pty-hub-attach.ts. No hub: sessionExists false or clientSize null -> null; re-check the registry synchronously after the awaits; else create a hub {pty:null, clients:new Set(), cols, rows, pendingInput:[], inputClient:null, clientStates:new Map()}, register it, attachHubPty(deps.spawn(...)). Register the listener BEFORE capturing; buffer onData until the snapshot is sent; emit {kind:'snapshot', cols: hub.cols, rows: hub.rows, data: captureViewport} then one output with the buffered data; afterwards forward output/size; onExit -> {kind:'exit', code:null}. close() = removeHubListener(deps.hubs, sessionName, hub, listener) once, with the hub object captured when subscribing; nothing emitted after close. Production clientSize: tmuxExecAsync display-message '#{window_width},#{window_height},#{status}' with status off=+0, on=+1, digit n=+n, else null. Production captureViewport: capturePane(sessionName, 0, {escapeSequences:true}) with failure -> ''. Never call pty.write or pty.resize.

Add TerminalBridge resolving a shared conversation's terminal to a Herdr observe stream or the tmux hub

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5. Create src/dashboard/server/sharing/terminal-bridge.ts: TerminalSink {send(TerminalPayload)}, TerminalTarget (herdr terminalId | tmux sessionName | missing), TerminalBridgeDeps {resolveTarget, observeHerdr, subscribeTmux}, class TerminalBridge(conversationName, deps) with attach(sink): Promise<() => void> and close(), terminalPayloadOf(frame, sawSnapshot), productionTerminalBridgeDeps(). Per attach: missing or resolver throws -> one unavailable terminal_not_found, no-op detach. herdr -> observeHerdr(terminalId), pump frames with for-await: snapshot/output/size map 1:1; exit or iterator end -> unavailable terminal_not_found if no snapshot seen, else terminal_ended, then stop. tmux -> subscribeTmux with the same mapping; null -> terminal_not_found. Detach idempotent; detach during opening closes the source once open; a throwing sink is detached. close() detaches all; later attaches send nothing. Production resolveTarget: runDashboardDbJob('getConversationByName', name) -> conv.tmuxSession; resolveHerdrTerminalId(tmuxSession) -> herdr; else Effect.runPromise(sessionExists(tmuxSession)).catch(()=>false) -> tmux; else missing. observeHerdr = observeTerminal(id) with NO cols/rows. subscribeTmux = subscribeToTmuxHub. No write method anywhere; no logging.

items.title: Given resolveTarget answers missing or throws, when attach runs, then the sink receives exactly one { kind: 'unavailable', reason: 'terminal_not_found' }
Given a herdr target whose observation yields snapshot, output and size frames, when attach runs, then the sink receives snapshot, output and size payloads in that order

Given a herdr observation that exits after a snapshot, when the exit frame arrives, then the sink receives unavailable terminal_ended; if it exits before any snapshot, then unavailable terminal_not_found

Given two attaches on a herdr target, when each is detached and then close() is called, then two observations were opened, each close() was called once, frames after detach are not delivered, and an attach after close() sends nothing
Given a tmux target, when subscribeTmux returns null, then the sink receives terminal_not_found; when it returns a subscription, then frames map identically and detach calls its close()

metadata.acJustification: Six criteria: the five behaviour checks plus the loopback test's required dep update, which otherwise breaks at runtime.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-6. PeerHubDeps gains terminal: {attach(sink: TerminalSink): Promise<() => void>; close(): void}; productionPeerHubDeps adds new TerminalBridge(conversationName, productionTerminalBridgeDeps()). PeerEntry gains terminalWatch=false, terminalGeneration=0, detachTerminal=null. Keep line 282 unchanged (no onMessage on terminal) and comment that read-only is structural. onControlMessage: kind 'terminal-watch' is honoured only when helloState === 'negotiated' and watch is boolean -> setTerminalWatch. setTerminalWatch: same value -> no-op; true -> maybeAttachTerminal; false -> bump generation, call+clear detachTerminal. maybeAttachTerminal requires not closed, negotiated, terminalWatch, open.has('terminal'), detachTerminal null; capture generation=++terminalGeneration; attach({send: p => sendTerminal(entry, generation, p)}).then(detach => stale or closed ? detach() : store). sendTerminal drops stale generations, else sendEnvelope(entry,'terminal',p) swallowing RangeError. onChannelOpen: 'terminal' -> maybeAttachTerminal. closePeer bumps generation and detaches; close() calls deps.terminal.close(). Update the module header. In peer-hub.test.ts replace the line-553 case 'never writes to or reads from drafts and terminal' (drafts stays silent; terminal sends only after a watch) and add a fake terminal dep; peer-hub-loopback.test.ts builds PeerHubDeps at line 95: add `terminal: { attach: async () => () => undefined, close: () => undefined }` there, otherwise hub.close() throws on the missing dep at runtime.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7. WebRtcViewerCallbacks gains onTerminal(payload: TerminalPayload). Negotiation gains control: RTCDataChannel | null and controlSeq (hello reply is seq 1). wireChannel (line 227) wires 'terminal' as well; only 'drafts' stays unwired. Terminal envelopes are accepted only when negotiation.streamId is set and equal; export readTerminalPayload(value): rebuild field by field, cols/rows safe integers 1..1000, data string, reason one of the two, else null (dropped). Add SharedTerminalView: a read-only xterm sized to the host terminal

narrative.Action: PRD WI-8. Create SharedTerminalView({ watch }) where watch(listener) => stop. On mount: new Terminal({ disableStdin: true, cursorBlink: false, cursorInactiveStyle: 'none', scrollback: 0, convertEol: false, fontSize: 14, fontFamily: resolved --font-mono (same lookup as XTerminal.tsx), theme: {...palette} }), open into the container, then stop = watch(onPayload). No FitAddon, no WebglAddon, no onData/onKey/attachCustomKeyEventHandler. Unmount: stop(), dispose(). snapshot -> reset(); resize(cols, rows); write(data) and clear any notice; output -> write; size -> resize; unavailable -> notice text ('The host's terminal is not running.' for terminal_not_found, 'The host's terminal session ended.' for terminal_ended). Palette from useTheme/useColorTheme like XTerminal.tsx lines 101-114; a palette change sets term.options.theme. Root <div data-testid="shared-terminal" className="min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto bg-background p-2"> with caption 'Read-only — you are watching the host's terminal.'. Do not modify XTerminal.tsx. Mock @xterm/xterm as XTerminal.test.tsx does. Add the test path to scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt in sorted position.
